question: (x+(1)/(x)) (x-(1)/(x)) (x²+(1)/(x²)) (x⁴+(1)/(x⁴)) is equal to:
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Apply the algebraic identity **(a + b)(a − b) = a² − b²** successively.

(x + 1/x)(x − 1/x) = x² − 1/x²

(x² − 1/x²)(x² + 1/x²) = x⁴ − 1/x⁴

(x⁴ − 1/x⁴)(x⁴ + 1/x⁴) = x⁸ − 1/x⁸

**∴ The correct answer is x⁸ − 1/x⁸.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** (x + 1/x)(x − 1/x)(x² + 1/x²)(x⁴ + 1/x⁴)

**Formula Used:** Difference of squares **(a + b)(a − b) = a² − b²**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/30603d37c1c675bcc774863acd4c06ed3838693f368fed35467ba1f5268286ed.png] 

⇒ Step 1: Multiply (x + 1/x) and (x − 1/x) = x² − (1/x)² = x² − 1/x²

⇒ Step 2: Multiply result with (x² + 1/x²) = (x²)² − (1/x²)² = x⁴ − 1/x⁴

⇒ Step 3: Multiply result with (x⁴ + 1/x⁴) = (x⁴)² − (1/x⁴)² = x⁸ − 1/x⁸

**∴ The correct answer is x⁸ − 1/x⁸.**

**__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identities

Standard identity: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² and (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b².

Power Rule

When multiplying terms with the same base, add exponents: xa × xb = xa⁺b. For powers: (xa)b = xa×b.

Successive Application

The pattern (x − 1)(x + 1)(x² + 1)...(xⁿ + 1) always results in x²ⁿ − 1.</p
